programme: No single recognizable module spans these twelve factors. The only factor with an unambiguous identity is RFX5, whose target list (CIITA plus HLA-E, HLA-F, HLA-DMA/DMB/DOA/DOB/DPA1/DPB1/DQB2/DRA, 9/17 ReMap-bound) is the classic RFX5 MHC class II transactivation signature. Nothing else in the list corroborates or extends it: HCFC1/PML/ASXL1/KLF7 point toward a cell-cycle checkpoint and senescence axis (CDKN1A, CDKN1B, CDKN2A, CDKN2B, E2F1, E2F4, TP53, BAX, CASP3, CCNA2, CDC6); KLF7/ATOH1 point toward neurotrophin and sensory differentiation signaling (NGF, NTRK1, NTRK2, BDNF); ZFPM1 is a hematopoietic GATA cofactor; AEBP1 is adipogenic/fibrotic; CREB3, EHF, ZNF423, FOXJ3 are epithelial, UPR, and neurodevelopmental factors with no overlap to the others. These are separate, mutually unconnected programmes, not one module.
role_in_a: If anything, RFX5-driven MHC class II presentation would relate to immune recognition of urothelial tumor cells (relevant to BCG immunotherapy biology), but that link is not established by anything retrieved here — Open Targets records no RFX5 association with Bladder_Cancer and no paper was retrieved for it.
role_in_b: No role is attested. Open Targets records no RFX5 association with Fibromyalgia, and no paper was retrieved for it in either disease.
shared_axis: None can be stated. RFX5's MHC-II identity is real but isolated — no second factor reinforces it, and neither disease record places RFX5 in it. The other eleven factors split across at least four unrelated processes (cell-cycle/senescence, neurotrophin signaling, hematopoietic/adipogenic differentiation, epithelial/UPR/zinc-finger developmental programmes) that do not converge on each other or on a plausible bladder–fibromyalgia mechanism.
reasoning: Twelve co-recurring factors do not by themselves make a mechanism, and here they fragment into several disjoint, individually plausible but mutually unrelated programmes rather than one. The only factor with a clean, nameable identity (RFX5/MHC-II) has zero retrieved or database support in either disease, and the record explicitly states no shared mechanism was found. Constructing a story here would mean picking one sub-cluster (e.g., the cell-cycle module) and asserting it explains fibromyalgia despite total silence on that side — exactly the overreach the exclusions are meant to guard against.
support: PMID 41457631 — places HCFC1 in Bladder_Cancer (intravesical delivery study), bladder-only, no fibromyalgia counterpart. PMID 31966702 — places ASXL1 in Bladder_Cancer via circASXL1 and TNM stage, bladder-only. PMID 40612002 — places AEBP1 in Bladder_Cancer via AEBP1-GLI1/FACT complex, bladder-only. PMID 41836296 — places AEBP1 in a bladder cancer molecular subtyping study, bladder-only. PMID 30723390 — places AEBP1 among bladder cancer stage-associated hub genes (WGCNA), bladder-only. PMID 37969188 — places PML in a bladder cancer arsenic gene-expression study, bladder-only. None of these touch fibromyalgia or a shared axis.
how_to_falsify: Take RFX5 occupancy and HLA-DR/MHC-II expression in matched bladder tumor tissue and fibromyalgia peripheral blood mononuclear cells, and separately assay the CDKN1A/CDKN1B/CDKN2A/CDKN2B–E2F1/E2F4–TP53 checkpoint module's activity in the same two sample sets; if either shows coordinated, disease-relevant dysregulation in both conditions, that would overturn the 'incoherent' call and justify building a real shared-axis account around whichever module holds up.
caveats: 100 patient-group comparisons but only 1 independent cohort pair, so the concordance is not independently replicated — it is one comparison scored many ways. Blood is heavily pre-filtered: CIITA, STAT1, IRF4, BCL6, LEF1, KLF2/9, DNMT1, SPIB and HLX were all removed as tissue-generic, stripping out exactly the immune regulators (including RFX5's own canonical partner CIITA) that would be needed to turn the RFX5 fragment into a real antigen-presentation story. No factor here has any Open Targets or literature association with Fibromyalgia at all; every retrieved paper that placed a factor in a disease placed it in Bladder_Cancer only. The single-view exclusions (ATF3, EZH2, FUS, PBX1, etc.) confirm this isn't a subgroup-driven artifact, but that only means the twelve factors that do recur still fail to cohere — recurrence alone did not produce a mechanism.
